analysis.description: The paper proposes Latent Variable Sequential Set Transformers, referred to as AutoBots, a novel encoder-decoder architecture for generating scene-consistent multi-agent trajectories. It demonstrates robust multi-modal prediction capabilities across various trajectory prediction benchmarks, including nuScenes, Argoverse, and TrajNet++, using both temporal and social self-attention modules.

type.justification: The paper conducts experiments on multiple datasets to demonstrate the effectiveness of its proposed model (AutoBot) under various conditions, using performance metrics and comparisons to other methods.
type.quote: We evaluate AutoBot on nuScenes (Caesar et al., 2020) and Argoverse (Chang et al., 2019), two autonomous driving trajectory prediction benchmarks, on the synthetic partition of the TrajNet++ (Kothari et al., 2021) dataset, a pedestrian trajectory forecasting benchmark, and Omniglot (Lake et al., 2015).

name.justification: The paper focuses on predicting the trajectories of multiple agents in a scene, utilizing advanced transformer-based architectures to handle the complexity of multi-agent systems.
name.quote: Robust multi-agent trajectory prediction is essential for the safe control of robotic systems.

name.justification: The paper applies its models to datasets specifically curated for autonomous driving scenarios, such as nuScenes and Argoverse, to test the efficacy of its motion prediction.
name.quote: In subsection 4.1 we show strong performance on the competitive motion-prediction dataset nuScenes (Caesar et al., 2020), a dataset recorded from a self-driving car.

name.justification: The paper directly addresses how to foresee future positions of agents in a given scene, fitting well within the trajectory prediction discipline.
name.quote: A major challenge is to efficiently learn a representation that approximates the true joint distribution of contextual, social, and temporal information to enable planning.

name.justification: By concentrating on trajectory prediction for joint multi-agent systems, the research is applicable to robotic systems that require precise motion forecasting.
name.quote: Robust multi-agent trajectory prediction is essential for the safe control of robotic systems.

name.justification: AutoBot is explicitly introduced as the novel model proposed by the paper, encompassing advanced attention mechanisms to handle multi-agent trajectory prediction.
name.quote: In this work, we propose this type of parameterized conditional mixture model over sequences of sets, and call this model a Latent Variable Sequential Set Transformer (affectionately referred to as ‘AutoBot’).

is_contributed.justification: AutoBot is introduced as a key innovation of the paper, specifically designed to enhance multi-agent motion trajectory prediction.
is_contributed.quote: We propose Latent Variable Sequential Set Transformers which are encoder-decoder architectures that generate scene-consistent multi-agent trajectories. We refer to these architectures as ‘AutoBots’.

is_executed.justification: The paper mentions the computational efficiency of AutoBot, including its ability to train on a single desktop GPU, suggesting execution on a GPU.
is_executed.quote: A distinguishing feature of AutoBots is that all models are trainable on a single desktop GPU (1080 Ti) in under 48h.

is_compared.justification: AutoBot's performance is compared against other existing models across various benchmarks, notably achieving top results in some metrics.
is_compared.quote: For the single-agent prediction case, our model achieves top results on the global nuScenes vehicle motion prediction leaderboard, and produces strong results on the Argoverse vehicle prediction challenge.

is_contributed.quote: Note, that in the appendix C, we present the computational complexity of AutoBot-Ego compared to WIMP (Khandelwal et al., 2020), which shows a 2x inference speedup.
